knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be agents, \(G^k=(V,E^k)\) a communication graph, and \(W^k\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) a mixing matrix. Agent states are stacked as \(x^k=(x_1^k,\ldots,x_m^k)\in(\mathbb R^d)^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition captures the graph, algebraic mixing, and message-locality data underlying distributed iterations, without committing to a particular optimization update or convergence regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed information-propagation structure is a sequence \[\mathfrak P=((G^k,W^k,\mathcal M^k))_{k\ge0}\] satisfying the locality condition \[w_{ij}^k\ne0\ \Longrightarrow\ j=i\ \text{or}\ (j,i)\in E^k,\] together with message rules under which agent \(i\)'s received information at round \(k\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_i^k=\prod_{j:(j,i)\in E^k}\mathcal M_{ji}^k\). Its linear propagation operator on vector-valued node states is \(W^k\otimes I_d\), and propagation over rounds \(s,\ldots,k\) is represented by \[W^{k:s}=W^kW^{k-1}\cdots W^s.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed information-propagation structure specifies the communication graph, graph-compatible mixing matrix, and admissible neighbor messages at every round. For vector-valued states, one-step linear propagation is the Kronecker lift of the mixing matrix, and multi-round propagation is the ordered product of the round matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak P=((G^k,W^k,\mathcal M^k))_{k\ge0}\) with \(\operatorname{supp}(W^k)\) subordinate to \(E^k\cup\{(i,i):i\in V\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The locality implication is equivalent to \(\operatorname{supp}(W^k)\subseteq I\cup E^k\), using the convention that column \(j\) sends to row \(i\).
special_cases_latex: For a static network, \(G^k=G\) and possibly \(W^k=W\) for every \(k\).
Pure message passing need not be linear; setting \(W^k\) aside leaves the same graph-local message spaces.
immediate_consequences_latex: An entry \((W^{k:s})_{ij}\ne0\) records a possible time-respecting influence of node \(j\) on node \(i\).
Graph connectivity and matrix contraction are distinct properties and must be imposed separately in convergence results.
boundary_notes: Row-stochasticity, column-stochasticity, positivity, and connectivity are not included unless separately specified.
The orientation convention for \(E^k\) must be kept fixed when interpreting matrix entries.

children.top_down_role: Graph classes that delimit distributed convergence theory.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). A communication history is a finite or infinite sequence \(\mathbf G=(G^k)_{k\ge0}\) of directed graphs \(G^k=(V,E^k)\); an undirected graph is represented by reciprocal directed edges.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A regime is a class of admissible communication histories. The definition separates fixed topology, deterministic temporal variation, random activation, and unreliable realized communication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A communication-graph regime is a set \(\mathfrak G\subseteq\prod_{k\ge0}\mathcal G(V)\), optionally equipped with a probability law when its elements are random. A distributed method is admissible for the regime only if its round-\(k\) messages use edges in \(E^k\). Canonical subclasses are: static, when every \(\mathbf G\in\mathfrak G\) satisfies \(G^k=G\); dynamic, when \(G^k\) may vary but satisfies a stated temporal-connectivity condition; randomized activation, when \(G^k\) is a graph-valued random variable generated by an activation law; and unreliable communication, when \(E^k\) is obtained from attempted edges by a failure process.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A communication-graph regime is a set, or probability space, of graph sequences allowed by a distributed model. It determines which communication edges may be used at each round. Static, dynamic, randomized-activation, and unreliable regimes differ in how their graph sequences are generated and constrained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak G\subseteq\mathcal G(V)^{\mathbb N_0}\), and admissible round-\(k\) communication is supported on the realized edge set \(E^k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A regime may equivalently be specified by a constraint set on edge-indicator sequences \((\mathbf 1_{\{e\in E^k\}})_{e,k}\).
special_cases_latex: A singleton containing a constant graph sequence is a static regime.
An i.i.d. law on a finite collection of subgraphs is a randomized activation regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: Convergence claims over \(\mathfrak G\) must state whether they hold for every admissible history, almost surely, in probability, or in expectation.
A graph class alone does not determine mixing weights or message contents.
boundary_notes: Connectivity is not automatic; it must be encoded in the defining constraints on \(\mathfrak G\).
Random communication failures and intentional randomized activation can induce the same graph law but represent different system mechanisms.

notation.meaning: Collection of directed graphs on vertex set \(V\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A static undirected network has fixed reciprocal links; compatible mixing matrices use only self-weights and weights on those links.

eq j\) and \(\{i,j\}

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite simple graph with \(E\subseteq\{\{i,j\}:i,j\in V,\ i\ne j\}\). Communication occurs at rounds \(k\in\mathbb N_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The regime has a fixed reciprocal topology. Connectivity, weights, delays, and reliability are separate properties unless explicitly appended.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A communication regime is a static undirected network when there exists one undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) such that for every round \(k\), the available communication graph equals \(G^k=G\), and \[\{i,j\}\in E\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad i\text{ may send to }j\text{ and }j\text{ may send to }i.\] The neighbor set is time independent, \(N_i=\{j:\{i,j\}\in E\}\). The regime is connected static undirected when every pair of vertices is joined by a finite path in \(G\), equivalently when \(G\) has exactly one connected component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A static undirected network uses the same finite graph at every communication round, and every edge permits reciprocal communication. Each agent therefore has a fixed neighbor set. Connectivity is an additional qualification requiring a path between every pair of agents.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall k)\ G^k=G\) and \(\{i,j\}\in E\) represents both directed communication possibilities \((i,j)\) and \((j,i)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using a symmetric adjacency matrix \(A\), the regime satisfies \(A^k=A=(A)^\top\) for every \(k\).
For an undirected Laplacian \(L\), connectedness is equivalent to \(\ker L=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\).
special_cases_latex: A complete graph gives all-to-all reciprocal communication.
A tree is a connected static undirected network with \(m-1\) edges.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any matrix with graph-compatible sparsity has a time-independent permitted support.
Reciprocal availability does not require equal weights in the two communication directions unless symmetry is separately imposed.
boundary_notes: Self-loops are conventions for local state retention and are not edges of the simple graph.
Static topology does not exclude asynchronous execution or message delay.

notation.meaning: Fixed set of neighbors of agent \(i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Static Directed Networks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A static directed network has fixed asymmetric arcs; an agent's update may use only its own state and messages from its in-neighbors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A static directed network is a fixed digraph \(G=(V,A)\), where \((j,i)\in A\) means that agent \(j\) can send information to agent \(i\). Accordingly, \(N_i^-=\{j:(j,i)\in A\}\) and \(N_i^+=\{j:(i,j)\in A\}\), and these sets need not coincide. A compatible update matrix \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfies \(W_{ij}=0\) for \(j\neq i\) whenever \((j,i)\notin A\). For information from every agent to influence every other agent, the fixed digraph must be strongly connected, unless a weaker rooted objective is explicitly intended.
assumptions_latex: \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is fixed and finite.
Directed communication links do not change with iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is a static directed communication network.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed finite asymmetric communication graph with sender-to-receiver arc convention.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite directed graph with \(E\subseteq V\times V\). The convention \((j,i)\in E\) means that agent \(j\) can send information to agent \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The regime has a fixed potentially asymmetric topology. Strong connectivity, weight balance, and stochastic mixing conventions are additional qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A communication regime is a static directed network when one directed graph \(G=(V,E)\) satisfies \[G^k=G\quad\text{for every round }k.\] The time-independent in- and out-neighbor sets are \[N_i^- =\{j:(j,i)\in E\},\qquad N_i^+=\{j:(i,j)\in E\}.\] Reciprocity is not required: \((j,i)\in E\) need not imply \((i,j)\in E\). The network is strongly connected when, for every ordered pair \((j,i)\), a directed path from \(j\) to \(i\) exists in \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A static directed network uses one fixed directed graph at every round. An edge records one-way communication, so an agent's in-neighbors and out-neighbors may differ. Strong connectivity is the additional property that every agent can influence every other through a directed path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall k)\ G^k=G\), with fixed \(N_i^-\) and \(N_i^+\), and no reciprocity requirement on \(E\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Strong connectivity is equivalent to irreducibility of the nonnegative adjacency matrix under the stated edge orientation.
A static undirected network is the special case in which \((i,j)\in E\Longleftrightarrow(j,i)\in E\).
special_cases_latex: A directed cycle is strongly connected and generally asymmetric.
A rooted directed graph need not be strongly connected; it only requires a root with paths to all vertices.
immediate_consequences_latex: A graph-compatible mixing matrix may be nonsymmetric.
In-neighbor and out-neighbor information requirements can lead to row-stochastic, column-stochastic, or push-sum constructions.
boundary_notes: Strong connectivity is not part of the unqualified static directed definition.
The edge orientation convention must be stated because some literature uses the transpose convention.

notation.meaning: Agents that can send directly to \(i\).
Agents that can receive directly from \(i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniformly jointly connected dynamic network regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and let \(G^k=(V,E^k)\) be a graph sequence. For integers \(s\le t\), define the union graph \(G^{[s,t]}=(V,\bigcup_{k=s}^tE^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The canonical regime permits arbitrary per-round disconnection but requires connectivity to accumulate uniformly over bounded time windows. Both undirected and directed variants are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A graph sequence \((G^k)_{k\ge0}\) is a dynamic network. It is \(B\)-jointly connected in the undirected case if some integer \(B\ge1\) satisfies \[G^{[s,s+B-1]}\text{ is connected for every }s\ge0.\] In the directed case it is \(B\)-jointly strongly connected when every such union graph is strongly connected; a weaker rooted variant requires every window union to contain a directed spanning tree. A dynamic network regime is uniformly jointly connected when one common finite \(B\) works for every graph history admitted by the regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic network is a sequence of communication graphs. Uniform joint connectivity allows an individual round to be disconnected, but requires the union of every fixed-length window to be connected. Directed variants use either strong connectivity or the weaker existence of a directed spanning tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\exists B\ge1)(\forall s\ge0)\ G^{[s,s+B-1]}\) satisfies the selected undirected, strongly directed, or rooted connectivity condition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For undirected graphs, \(B\)-joint connectivity means that every nontrivial cut is crossed by at least one active edge during each window of \(B\) consecutive rounds.
special_cases_latex: A connected static graph is \(1\)-jointly connected.
A periodic graph sequence is jointly connected when the union over each aligned and shifted window of a suitable bounded length is connected.
immediate_consequences_latex: Information may traverse different edges at different times even when no single \(G^k\) is connected.
Window-union connectivity alone does not specify mixing weights or their lower bounds.
boundary_notes: Connectivity of the union ignores temporal edge order; some directed propagation results require stronger time-respecting conditions.
The unqualified dynamic family includes sequences that are not jointly connected; uniform joint connectivity is a named subregime.

notation.meaning: Graph formed by the union of edges active from round \(s\) through \(t\).

review_flags: The bounded-window definition is standard but lacks an inspected supporting locator.

Time-Varying Graph Sequences
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A time-varying network keeps the agent set fixed while its communication links, and hence its compatible mixing matrix, may change each iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A time-varying graph sequence is \(\mathcal G=(G_t)_{t\geq0}\), where every \(G_t=(V,E_t)\) has the same finite vertex set \(V\), while the edge or arc set \(E_t\) may change with \(t\). Communication performed at time \(t\) must respect \(E_t\): a compatible mixing matrix \(W_t\) has \((W_t)_{ij}=0\) whenever \(j\neq i\) and the link from \(j\) to \(i\) is absent from \(E_t\). The sequence may be deterministic, stochastic, or generated by a switching signal; those regimes require additional assumptions beyond this definition.
assumptions_latex: \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is fixed while communication may vary over discrete times \(t\in\mathbb{N}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G=(G_t)_{t\geq0}\) is a time-varying graph sequence on common vertex set \(V\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time graph sequence with fixed agents and changing communication edges.

notation.meaning: Communication graph active at time t

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and correctly keeps deterministic, stochastic, and switching assumptions outside the basic graph-sequence definition. However, no inspectable source is supplied for the dynamic-network formulation or its time-indexed mixing-matrix support condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Topology-Switching Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A switching regime selects each active communication graph from a finite family using a signal that may obey dwell-time or transition restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A topology-switching regime is represented by a finite graph family \(\{G^{(1)},\ldots,G^{(M)}\}\) and a switching signal \(\sigma:\mathbb{N}\to\{1,\ldots,M\}\), with active graph \(G_t=G^{(\sigma(t))}\). If each mode has a compatible mixing matrix \(W^{(m)}\), then the communication update uses \(W_t=W^{(\sigma(t))}\). The admissible switching class is a specified set \(\Sigma\) of signals; it may impose dwell time, transition constraints, or connectivity conditions. Arbitrary switching is the special case in which \(\Sigma\) contains every signal with values in \(\{1,\ldots,M\}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\{G^{(1)},\ldots,G^{(M)}\}\) is a finite family of graphs on the same vertex set \(V\).
\(\sigma:\mathbb{N}\to\{1,ldots,M\}\) is a switching signal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active topology satisfies \(G_t=G^{(\sigma(t))}\) for every \(t\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-mode discrete-time switching representation; dwell-time restrictions are optional additions.

notation.meaning: Mixing matrix assigned to mode m

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the appropriate role and the statement itself gives a coherent finite-mode switching model. Nevertheless, no source supports the formulation, and the second assumption contains malformed LaTeX, using 1,ldots,M instead of 1,\ldots,M. A sourced corrected record is required.

children.top_down_role: Random edge, node, or subgraph activation regimes.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space, \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0}\) a filtration, and \(G_0=(V,E_0)\) a base communication graph. At round \(k\), an activation variable \(A_k\) selects nodes, edges, or a subgraph.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns intentional stochastic selection of communication opportunities. Independence and identical distribution are optional special assumptions, not part of the general family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A randomized activation network is a graph-valued stochastic process \[G^k=(V,E^k),\qquad E^k=\Psi(A_k)\subseteq E_0,\] where \(A_k\) is \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable and its conditional law given \(\mathcal F_k\) is specified by an activation kernel \(K_k(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_k)\). Edge activation has persistent conditional support if constants \(p_e>0\) satisfy \[\mathbb P(e\in E^k\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p_e\quad\text{a.s. for every }e\in E_0\text{ and }k.\] Node activation is defined analogously, with \(E^k\) induced by the selected node set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized activation network is a stochastic sequence of subgraphs of a base graph. A random activation variable selects nodes, edges, or whole subgraphs according to a conditional probability kernel. Persistent support means every base edge has a uniformly positive conditional probability of activation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G^k=\Psi(A_k)\subseteq G_0\) is graph-valued and governed by the conditional activation kernel \(K_k(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For edge activation, indicators \(\delta_e^k=\mathbf1_{\{e\in E^k\}}\) specify the realized graph through \(E^k=\{e\in E_0:\delta_e^k=1\}\).
special_cases_latex: Randomized gossip selects one edge at each round.
Independent Bernoulli edge activation uses mutually independent indicators with \(\mathbb P(\delta_e^k=1)=p_e\).
Random-coordinate communication activates the subgraph associated with a sampled block or agent.
immediate_consequences_latex: Convergence statements must specify their probabilistic mode.
Positive marginal activation probabilities do not imply independence or bounded waiting times.
boundary_notes: An adversarially chosen graph sequence is not randomized unless a probability law is part of the model.
Random packet loss may induce the same mathematics but belongs to an unreliable-network mechanism when attempted transmissions fail.

notation.meaning: Conditional probability kernel governing activation at round \(k\).
Indicator that edge \(e\) is active at round \(k\).

review_flags: No inspected source establishes the stated general conditional-kernel definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized activation network
Random Graph Activation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round the active communication graph is random, and the realized update may use only links activated in that round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A random graph activation process is a sequence of graph-valued random variables \(G_t=(V,E_t)\). Equivalently, for each admissible link \(e\), the indicator \(A_e^t=\mathbf 1\{e\in E_t\}\) is a random variable measurable with respect to the round history \(\mathcal F_t\). A communication or mixing matrix \(W_t\) is admissible only if \((W_t)_{ij}=0\) whenever the corresponding link from \(j\) to \(i\) is inactive at time \(t\). Independence across links or times, identical activation probabilities, and positive lower probability bounds are additional regime assumptions, not parts of the basic definition.
assumptions_latex: \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is fixed and \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) is a probability space.
Communication occurs at discrete times \(t\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((G_t)_{t\geq0}\) is a random graph activation process, and each update must be supported on the realized \(G_t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time random edge activation without imposing independence or identical distributions.

notation.meaning: Random active graph at time t

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits random graph activation and appropriately leaves independence and probability bounds as additional assumptions. No source is supplied, and the meaning of the history sigma-field F_t must specify whether it includes the round-t realization before asserting that A_e^t is F_t-measurable.

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Gossip Networks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sampled edge averages its two endpoint states while every other node retains its state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let each node hold \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\). At iteration \(k\), sample an edge \(e_k=\{i,j\}\) with probability \(p_{ij}>0\). Its endpoints update by \(x_i^{k+1}=x_j^{k+1}=(x_i^k+x_j^k)/2\), while \(x_\ell^{k+1}=x_\ell^k\) for \(\ell\notin\{i,j\}\). Equivalently, with stacked state \(x^k\), \[x^{k+1}=\left(W_{ij}\otimes I_d\right)x^k,\qquad W_{ij}=I_n-\tfrac12(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^\top.\] The running convention outputs \(x^k\); a finite implementation may stop when a prescribed disagreement measure is below tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is fixed and undirected.
\(p_{ij}>0\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=(W_{e_k}\otimes I_d)x^k\) and \(\sum_i x_i^{k+1}=\sum_i x_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical randomized edge-activated averaging on a fixed undirected graph.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Activated Gossip
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An activated node chooses a neighbor, and the selected pair averages its states while every other node retains its state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let node \(i\) hold \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\). Define the stacked state \(x^k=(x_1^k,\ldots,x_n^k)\in(\mathbb R^d)^n\). At iteration \(k\), sample an active node \(i_k\) with probability \(q_i>0\), then sample \(j_k\in N(i_k)\) with conditional probability \(r_{j\mid i}>0\). Nodes \(i_k\) and \(j_k\) replace their states by their arithmetic mean, and all other states remain unchanged. Thus \[x^{k+1}=\left(\left[I_n-\tfrac12(e_{i_k}-e_{j_k})(e_{i_k}-e_{j_k})^\top\right]\otimes I_d\right)x^k,\] where \(e_i\) is the \(i\)-th standard basis vector of \(\mathbb R^n\). The current stacked state is the output, with optional termination at a chosen disagreement tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Every node has at least one neighbor.
\(q_i r_{j\mid i}>0\) on every directed neighbor choice required for information propagation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update preserves \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^k\) and changes only the selected pair.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical node-clock gossip with one neighbor selected conditionally on the active node.

notation.meaning: probability of choosing neighbor \(j\) given active node \(i\)

knowledge_statements.title: Activation-Dependence Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activation laws may be independent, conditionally fixed-law, Markov, or generally history-dependent; convergence assumptions must match the chosen dependence class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\) denote the activated node, edge, or subgraph at time \(k\), and let \(\mathcal F_k=\sigma(A_0,\ldots,A_k)\). The activation process is independent when the variables \((A_k)_{k\ge0}\) are mutually independent; conditionally independent with fixed law when \(\mathbb P(A_k\in S\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})=\mu_k(S)\) almost surely for deterministic probability measures \(\mu_k\); Markov when \(\mathbb P(A_k\in S\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})=K_k(A_{k-1},S)\); and history-dependent otherwise. Any convergence claim for randomized communication must state which regime is assumed and impose connectivity or mixing conditions appropriate to that regime.
assumptions_latex: \((A_k)_{k\ge0}\) is defined on a common probability space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditional law \(\mathbb P(A_k\in\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\) determines the activation-dependence regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence classes for a sequence of random communication activations.
review_flags: Terminology and admissible dependence classes vary across distributed-optimization analyses.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the selected terminology. In particular, the stated deterministic conditional-law condition already entails independence from the activation history and is not clearly distinct from the preceding mutual-independence regime.

children.title: Unreliable Communication Graphs
children.top_down_role: Communication affected by packet loss, dropouts, or link failures.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G_0=(V,E_0)\) be a base graph. At round \(k\), \(T^k\subseteq E_0\) is the set of attempted transmissions and \(R^k\subseteq T^k\) is the set successfully received. Let \(D_e^k\in\{0,1\}\) indicate failure of attempted edge \(e\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This family models the discrepancy between attempted and delivered communication caused by packet loss, dropout, or link failure. Failure may be deterministic, stochastic, correlated, or state dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unreliable communication network is specified by \[(G_0,(T^k)_{k\ge0},(D_e^k)_{e\in E_0,k\ge0}),\] with realized edge sets \[R^k=\{e\in T^k:D_e^k=0\}.\] A message sent on \(e\in T^k\) is available to its receiver at round \(k\) exactly when \(e\in R^k\); otherwise the receiver applies a prescribed missing-message rule. In a stochastic bounded-loss model, constants \(q_e<1\) may satisfy \[\mathbb P(D_e^k=1\mid\mathcal F_k)\le q_e\quad\text{a.s.}\] In a deterministic bounded-burst model, each required edge succeeds at least once in every stated finite window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unreliable network distinguishes attempted transmissions from successful deliveries. A failure indicator removes attempted edges from the realized communication graph, after which the algorithm applies its specified missing-message behavior. Reliability assumptions may bound conditional loss probabilities or the duration of failure bursts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R^k=\{e\in T^k:D_e^k=0\}\subseteq T^k\subseteq E_0\), and only messages on \(R^k\) are delivered at round \(k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With adjacency masks, the realized communication matrix is \(W^k=M^k\odot\widehat W^k\), where \(\widehat W^k\) represents attempted links and \(M^k\) successful deliveries.

A complete link outage at round \(k\) is represented by \(R^k=\varnothing\).
Node dropout removes every attempted incident transmission associated with the unavailable node.

A convergence guarantee requires assumptions on the failure process and on how missing messages affect state updates.

A positive success probability alone does not guarantee uniform finite-window delivery.

Intermittent-Link Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Physical links may switch on and off; bounded intermittency requires every fixed-length union graph to remain connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a fixed physical graph. An intermittent-link regime is a sequence \((G_k)_{k\ge0}\) with \(G_k=(V,E_k)\) and \(E_k\subseteq E\), where an edge may alternate between available and unavailable states. Writing \(a_e(k)=\mathbf 1\{e\in E_k\}\), deterministic intermittency specifies the binary sequences \(a_e(k)\), whereas stochastic intermittency specifies their joint law relative to a filtration. A bounded-intermittency condition with window \(B\ge1\) requires \[\left(V,\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}E_t\right)\text{ to be connected for every }k.\] This condition permits disconnected instantaneous graphs while enforcing recurrent network-wide information paths.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is the fixed physical graph containing every possible active edge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Instantaneous disconnection is allowed, while \(B\)-window connectivity guarantees recurrent aggregate connectivity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-varying subgraph model in which fixed physical links may be temporarily unavailable.

knowledge_statements.title: Packet-Loss Networks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each directed transmission has a delivery indicator; its realized edges and missing-message rule define the packet-loss network seen by the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a nominal directed communication graph. For each \((i,j)\in E\) and time \(k\), let \(\delta_{ij}(k)\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether the packet sent by \(i\) is received by \(j\). The realized graph is \(G_k=(V,E_k)\), where \(E_k=\{(i,j)\in E:\delta_{ij}(k)=1\}\). A packet-loss network is the nominal graph together with the joint law, or deterministic specification, of \((\delta_{ij}(k))\). Losses may be asymmetric, correlated across links, and temporally dependent; any algorithm using missing messages must additionally specify whether a receiver skips, renormalizes, substitutes, or stores delayed information.
assumptions_latex: Packets are indexed by a discrete communication time \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_k=\{(i,j)\in E:\delta_{ij}(k)=1\}\) is the realized communication edge set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed message-delivery model allowing asymmetric loss on nominal communication links.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Dropout Networks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A participation indicator selects active nodes; strict dropouts communicate with nobody and retain their previous states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a fixed graph and let \(s_i(k)\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether node \(i\) participates at time \(k\). The active set is \(V_k=\{i\in V:s_i(k)=1\}\), and the realized communication graph is the induced graph \(G_k=G[V_k]\), unless a protocol explicitly retains edges to inactive nodes. In the strict-dropout convention, an inactive node sends no message, receives no message, and preserves its local state: \(x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k\) whenever \(s_i(k)=0\). The dropout process is specified by the deterministic sequence or joint probability law of \((s_i(k))\).
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) contains every communication link available when both endpoints participate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strict-dropout realized graph is \(G_k=G[V_k]\), and inactive states satisfy \(x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-varying participation model in which inactive nodes neither send nor receive updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Connectivity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If no cross-cut link recurs infinitely often, the two sides eventually cannot exchange information, preventing universal exact consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph sequence \(G_k=(V,E_k)\), define the persistent union \(G_\infty=(V,E_\infty)\) by \(E_\infty=\{e:e\in E_k\text{ for infinitely many }k\}\). If \(G_\infty\) is disconnected, choose a nonempty proper component \(S\subset V\). After some finite time no edge crossing \((S,V\setminus S)\) is activated. Consequently, any distributed protocol whose node updates depend only on local states and received messages cannot, for every initial condition, compute a consensus value that depends nontrivially on data from both sides of the cut. Thus connectivity of \(G_\infty\) is necessary for universal exact consensus, although it is not sufficient without quantitative recurrence and weight assumptions.
assumptions_latex: Updates use only locally stored information and messages delivered along active edges.
The required consensus value depends nontrivially on every node's initial datum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Universal exact consensus implies that \(G_\infty\) is connected.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic obstruction caused by permanent separation of a time-varying network.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected undirected graph with \(|V|=m\), choose an orientation, let \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times |E|}\) be its incidence matrix, and let \(L=BB^\top\). For node variables \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\), write \(x=\operatorname{col}(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition identifies the standard incidence, Laplacian, mixing, and subspace descriptions of exact consensus on a connected undirected graph. Directed graphs require modified algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A graph-algebra representation of agreement is any linear operator \(K\) on node space whose nullspace is the consensus subspace \[\mathcal C=\{\mathbf1\otimes z:z\in\mathbb R^d\}.\] For the connected undirected graph, canonical choices satisfy \[\ker(B^\top\otimes I_d)=\ker(L\otimes I_d)=\mathcal C.\] If \(W\) is symmetric and satisfies \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) with eigenvalue \(1\) simple, then also \[\ker((I-W)\otimes I_d)=\mathcal C.\] The associated disagreement space is \(\mathcal C^\perp=\{x:(\mathbf1^\top\otimes I_d)x=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph-algebra representation of agreement is a node-space linear operator whose nullspace consists exactly of consensus vectors. For a connected undirected graph, the transpose incidence operator, graph Laplacian, and a suitable mixing residual all encode the same consensus subspace. Its orthogonal complement is the disagreement space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker(B^\top\otimes I_d)=\ker(L\otimes I_d)=\ker((I-W)\otimes I_d)=\mathcal C\) under the stated connectedness and mixing conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\in\mathcal C\Longleftrightarrow(B^\top\otimes I_d)x=0\Longleftrightarrow(L\otimes I_d)x=0\).
For admissible \(W\), \(x\in\mathcal C\Longleftrightarrow(W\otimes I_d)x=x\).
special_cases_latex: For scalar node states, \(d=1\) and \(\mathcal C=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\).
Weighted positive edges replace \(L\) by \(B\Omega B^\top\) with diagonal \(\Omega\succ0\) without changing the nullspace.
immediate_consequences_latex: Disagreement can be measured by edge differences, Laplacian energy, or distance to \(\mathcal C\), subject to graph-dependent constants.
The smallest positive Laplacian eigenvalue quantifies conditioning on \(\mathcal C^\perp\).
boundary_notes: Disconnected graphs have a larger nullspace corresponding to componentwise consensus.
Nonsymmetric directed mixing matrices need left and right invariant vectors and are not covered by this exact equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Laplacian Consensus Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the positive-weight support graph is connected, stacked node states agree exactly when the graph Laplacian annihilates them; the Laplacian quadratic form is their weighted disagreement energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=(w_{ij})\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(w_{ij}=w_{ji}\ge0\) and \(w_{ii}=0\), and suppose the undirected positive-weight support graph with edges \(\{i,j\}\) such that \(w_{ij}>0\) is connected. Define \(D=\operatorname{diag}(\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij})\) and \(L=D-W\). For stacked node variables \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in(\mathbb R^d)^n\), \[(L\otimes I_d)x=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x_1=\cdots=x_n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=\mathbf 1_n\otimes z\text{ for some }z\in\mathbb R^d.\] Moreover, \[x^\top(L\otimes I_d)x=\tfrac12\sum_{i,j=1}^n w_{ij}\lVert x_i-x_j\rVert^2,\] so the Laplacian energy measures weighted disagreement and vanishes exactly on the consensus subspace.
assumptions_latex: The graph formed by the pairs satisfying \(w_{ij}>0\) is connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker(L\otimes I_d)=\{\mathbf 1_n\otimes z:z\in\mathbb R^d\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus subspace characterized as the nullspace of a connected graph Laplacian.

notation.meaning: symmetric matrix of nonnegative edge weights

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E,w)\) be a finite weighted undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), symmetric weights \(w_{ij}=w_{ji}\ge0\), weighted adjacency matrix \(A\), degree matrix \(D\), and Laplacian \(L=D-A\). Stack \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\) as \(x\in\mathbb R^{md}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns node-space consensus geometry for weighted undirected graphs. Exact global consensus is obtained when the graph is connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The graph-Laplacian consensus representation associates the disagreement operator \[\mathcal L=L\otimes I_d\] and energy \[\mathcal E_G(x)=\frac12x^\top\mathcal Lx=\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}\|x_i-x_j\|^2.\] A node vector is graph-consensual when \(\mathcal Lx=0\). If \(G\) is connected and every graph edge has positive weight, then this condition is exactly global agreement: \[\mathcal Lx=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x_1=\cdots=x_m\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=\mathbf1\otimes z\text{ for some }z\in\mathbb R^d.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The graph-Laplacian representation applies the graph Laplacian to stacked node variables. Its quadratic energy is the weighted sum of squared differences across edges. A vector is graph-consensual when the Laplacian annihilates it; on a connected positively weighted graph, this is equivalent to all node values being equal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal E_G(x)=\tfrac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}\|x_i-x_j\|^2\), and for connected \(G\), \(\ker(L\otimes I_d)=\{\mathbf1\otimes z:z\in\mathbb R^d\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For connected \(G\), \(x\) is consensual if and only if \(x^\top(L\otimes I_d)x=0\).
Consensus is equivalent to \(x\) belonging to the nullspace of \(L\otimes I_d\).
special_cases_latex: For the complete graph with uniform weights, Laplacian disagreement is proportional to deviation from the network average.
For a disconnected graph, \(\mathcal Lx=0\) means agreement only within each connected component.
immediate_consequences_latex: On the disagreement subspace, \(x^\top(L\otimes I_d)x\ge\lambda_2(L)\|x\|^2\) when \(G\) is connected.
The spectral gap \(\lambda_2(L)>0\) characterizes connectedness and network conditioning.

The normalized Laplacian is a nearby representation with different scaling.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected graph with an arbitrary orientation of each edge. Let \(B\in\mathbb R^{|V|\times|E|}\) have column \(b_e=e_i-e_j\) when oriented edge \(e\) points from \(j\) to \(i\). Let node variables be \(x\in\mathbb R^{|V|d}\) and edge variables be \(y\in\mathbb R^{|E|d}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The pair formalizes how node potentials produce edge differences and how edge quantities produce node divergences. It is orientation dependent in coordinates but orientation independent in its consensus and Laplacian content.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The node-edge representation pair induced by \(G\) is the pair of adjoint linear maps \[\mathcal D=B^\top\otimes I_d:\mathbb R^{|V|d}\to\mathbb R^{|E|d},\qquad \mathcal D^*=B\otimes I_d:\mathbb R^{|E|d}\to\mathbb R^{|V|d}.\] For an oriented edge \(e=(j\to i)\), \((\mathcal D x)_e=x_i-x_j\), while \(\mathcal D^*y\) is the signed node divergence of the edge vector \(y\). Their node-space composition is \[\mathcal D^*\mathcal D=(BB^\top)\otimes I_d=L\otimes I_d.\] Thus edgewise agreement is \(\mathcal D x=0\), and for connected \(G\) it is equivalent to global consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The node-edge pair consists of the lifted transpose incidence map and its adjoint. The first turns node values into oriented edge differences; the second turns edge values into signed node divergences. Composing them gives the block graph Laplacian. On a connected graph, zero edge differences are exactly global consensus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal D=B^\top\otimes I_d\), \(\mathcal D^*=B\otimes I_d\), and \(\mathcal D^*\mathcal D=L\otimes I_d\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\mathcal D x=0\Longleftrightarrow x_i=x_j\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in E\).
If \(G\) is connected, \(\ker\mathcal D=\{\mathbf1\otimes z:z\in\mathbb R^d\}\).
For every \(x,y\), \(\langle\mathcal D x,y\rangle=\langle x,\mathcal D^*y\rangle\).
special_cases_latex: Positive edge weights \(\Omega\) give weighted maps \((\Omega^{1/2}B^\top)\otimes I_d\) and weighted Laplacian \(B\Omega B^\top\otimes I_d\).
For \(d=1\), the maps reduce to the ordinary discrete gradient and divergence.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing an edge orientation multiplies the corresponding edge coordinate by \(-1\) but leaves \(BB^\top\) unchanged.
Edge-space dual variables naturally couple to node consensus constraints through \(\mathcal D^*\).
boundary_notes: Cycles create a nontrivial nullspace of \(B\) in edge space; edge variables are therefore not generally unique.
For directed graphs, the incidence construction remains available, but it does not encode asymmetric mixing by itself.

notation.meaning: Signed incidence column for oriented edge \(e\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The incidence transpose forms edge differences, the incidence matrix forms node divergence, and their weighted product is the graph Laplacian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Orient each edge of an undirected weighted graph \(G=(V,E,w)\) arbitrarily, and define \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) so the column for \(e=(i,j)\) is \(e_i-e_j\). With \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(w_e)\), the weighted Laplacian factorization is \[L=BQB^\top,\qquad L\otimes I_d=(B\otimes I_d)(Q\otimes I_d)(B^\top\otimes I_d).\]

Each edge is assigned one arbitrary orientation.

knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Space Decision Variables
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An edge decision vector induces zero-sum node imbalances through incidence divergence and serves naturally as a multiplier for edgewise consensus constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) be an oriented incidence matrix and let \(y=(y_e)_{e\in E}\in(\mathbb R^d)^m\) assign a decision vector to each edge. Its induced node-space vector is \[u=(B\otimes I_d)y,\qquad u_i=\sum_{e\text{ leaves }i}y_e-\sum_{e\text{ enters }i}y_e.\] Hence \((\mathbf 1_n^\top\otimes I_d)u=0\). In a Lagrangian for the consensus constraint \((B^\top\otimes I_d)x=0\), the edge multiplier \(y\) couples through \(\langle y,(B^\top\otimes I_d)x\rangle=\langle(B\otimes I_d)y,x\rangle\). Edge variables differing by an element of \(\ker(B\otimes I_d)\) induce the same node vector.

knowledge_statements.title: Cycle-Space Structure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycle flows have zero node divergence, have dimension edges minus vertices plus components, and are orthogonal to all incidence gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite graph with oriented incidence matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), the cycle space is \[\mathcal C(G)=\ker B=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:By=0\}.\] Its elements are divergence-free edge flows; reversing an edge orientation only changes the corresponding coordinate sign and not the underlying space. If the graph has \(c\) connected components, then \(\operatorname{rank}B=n-c\) and \(\dim\mathcal C(G)=m-n+c\). Under the Euclidean inner product, \[\mathcal C(G)=\left(\operatorname{im}B^\top\right)^\perp.\] For vector-valued edge variables, the cycle space becomes \(\ker(B\otimes I_d)=\mathcal C(G)\otimes\mathbb R^d\).
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite graph with \(n\) vertices, \(m\) edges, and \(c\) connected components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker B=(\operatorname{im}B^\top)^\perp\) and \(\dim\ker B=m-n+c\).

knowledge_statements.title: Mixing-Operator Representation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixing operator on stacked agent states
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(n\ge 2\) agents have states \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\), and stack them as \(X=(x_1^\top,\ldots,x_n^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^{nd}\). Let \(W=[w_{ij}]\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a nonnegative matrix whose permitted nonzero entries follow a communication graph.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, synchronous, linear communication with a single fixed mixing matrix; stochasticity and contraction conditions are not imposed by this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mixing operator induced by \(W\) is \(\mathcal W:=W\otimes I_d:\mathbb R^{nd}\to\mathbb R^{nd}\), defined by \[X^+=\mathcal W X,\qquad x_i^+=\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}x_j\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).\] If information may flow from agent \(j\) to agent \(i\) only when \((j,i)\) is an allowed directed edge, graph compatibility requires \(w_{ij}=0\) for every disallowed pair \((j,i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixing operator is the Kronecker lift of a nonnegative agent-level weight matrix. It maps a stacked state to a new stacked state whose component at agent i is the weighted sum of the states received from agents j. Graph compatibility means that a weight must vanish whenever the corresponding communication from j to i is unavailable.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(n\ge2\), \(d\ge1\), \(X=(x_1^\top,\ldots,x_n^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^{nd}\), and \(J:=\frac1n\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\). Equip \(\mathbb R^{nd}\) with its Euclidean inner product.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The network consensus subspace and disagreement subspace are \[\mathcal C:=\{\mathbf1\otimes z:z\in\mathbb R^d\},\qquad \mathcal C^\perp:=\{Y\in\mathbb R^{nd}:(\mathbf1^\top\otimes I_d)Y=0\}.\] Every \(X\in\mathbb R^{nd}\) has the unique orthogonal decomposition \[X=X_{\parallel}+X_{\perp},\qquad X_{\parallel}=(J\otimes I_d)X=\mathbf1\otimes\bar x,\qquad X_{\perp}=((I_n-J)\otimes I_d)X,\] where \(\bar x:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stacked network state decomposes uniquely into an aggregate consensus component, in which every agent holds the arithmetic average, and an orthogonal disagreement component whose agent blocks sum to zero. The corresponding projectors are the Kronecker lifts of J and I minus J.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb R^{nd}\) is block-partitioned into agent states \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\).
\(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top/n\) and orthogonality is Euclidean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb R^{nd}=\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal C^\perp\) and \(X=(J\otimes I_d)X+((I_n-J)\otimes I_d)X\) uniquely.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(X\in\mathcal C\) if and only if \(x_1=\cdots=x_n\).
\(X\in\mathcal C^\perp\) if and only if \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=0\).
special_cases_latex: For scalar states, \(d=1\), the decomposition is \(x=Jx+(I_n-J)x\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The disagreement norm \(\|((I_n-J)\otimes I_d)X\|\) is zero exactly at consensus.
The projectors satisfy \((J\otimes I_d)((I_n-J)\otimes I_d)=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate-Motion Component
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every stacked state uniquely and orthogonally splits into a replicated network average and a zero-sum disagreement component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(J:=\mathbf{1}_n\mathbf{1}_n^\top/n\), and define \(\mathcal C:=\{\mathbf{1}_n\otimes u:u\in\mathbb{R}^d\}\) and \(\mathcal C^\perp:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{nd}:(\mathbf{1}_n^\top\otimes I_d)z=0\}\). \(x\in\mathbb{R}^{nd}\)

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Error Modes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For symmetric average-preserving mixing, every disagreement vector decomposes uniquely into orthogonal network eigenmodes, each multiplied by its associated nonconsensus eigenvalue per communication round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(W=W^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(W\mathbf{1}_n=\mathbf{1}_n\), and define \(\mathcal C^\perp:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{nd}:(\mathbf{1}_n^\top\otimes I_d)z=0\}\). \(W=W^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\)
\(W\mathbf{1}_n=\mathbf{1}_n\)
\(e\in\mathcal C^\perp\)

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a fixed communication graph on \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(W=[w_{ij}]\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and let \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top/n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed, nonnegative, doubly stochastic mixing on a graph, with strict Euclidean contraction on the disagreement subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix \(W\) satisfies the canonical mixing-matrix conditions for \(G\) when \[w_{ij}\ge0,\quad w_{ij}=0\ \text{if }j\ne i\text{ and }(j,i)\notin E,\quad W\mathbf1=\mathbf1,\quad \mathbf1^\top W=\mathbf1^\top,\] and its disagreement contraction factor \[\sigma(W):=\|W-J\|_2\] satisfies \(\sigma(W)<1\). Equivalently, \(WJ=JW=J\) and \(W-J\) is a strict contraction in spectral norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An admissible contractive mixing matrix is nonnegative, respects the graph, preserves both constant vectors and arithmetic sums, and strictly contracts the subspace orthogonal to consensus. Its contraction factor is the spectral norm of W minus the averaging projector J.
assumptions_latex: \(n\ge2\) and \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
The graph convention is that \((j,i)\in E\) permits agent \(i\) to use agent \(j\)'s state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditions define a graph-compatible, average-preserving matrix with \(\|(W-J)y\|_2\le\sigma(W)\|y\|_2\) and \(\sigma(W)<1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under double stochasticity, \(W-J=(I_n-J)W(I_n-J)\).
The contraction condition is \(\sup_{y\ne0,\,\mathbf1^\top y=0}\|Wy\|_2/\|y\|_2<1\).
special_cases_latex: If \(W\) is symmetric, \(\sigma(W)=\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i(W)|\), with eigenvalues ordered so that \(\lambda_1(W)=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For block states, \(\|((W-J)\otimes I_d)X\|_2\le\sigma(W)\|((I_n-J)\otimes I_d)X\|_2\).
boundary_notes: Row- or column-stochastic matrices on directed graphs need different invariant projections and need not satisfy this definition.
Graph compatibility and stochasticity alone do not imply \(\sigma(W)<1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Doubly Stochastic Mixing Conditions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative matrix is doubly stochastic when every row and column sums to one; its mixing preserves consensus and the arithmetic average.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix \(W=(w_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is doubly stochastic when \[w_{ij}\ge 0,\qquad W\mathbf{1}_n=\mathbf{1}_n,\qquad \mathbf{1}_n^\top W=\mathbf{1}_n^\top.\] Consequently, \(W\otimes I_d\) fixes every consensus state and preserves the arithmetic average: for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^{nd}\), \[(\mathbf{1}_n^\top\otimes I_d)(W\otimes I_d)x=(\mathbf{1}_n^\top\otimes I_d)x.\]
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W\mathbf{1}_n=\mathbf{1}_n\) and \(\mathbf{1}_n^\top W=\mathbf{1}_n^\top\), with nonnegative entries.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative mixing that preserves both consensus and the arithmetic average.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G_k=(V,E_k)\) be a possibly time-varying directed graph on \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(W_k=[w_{ij}(k)]\in\mathbb R_+^{n\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A support and positive-weight admissibility family; stochastic orientation and graph connectivity must be specified separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \((W_k)_{k\ge0}\) has graph-admissible, uniformly nondegenerate weights if there exists \(\eta\in(0,1]\) such that for every \(k\), \[w_{ij}(k)=0\quad\text{whenever }j\ne i\text{ and }(j,i)\notin E_k,\] \[w_{ij}(k)\ge\eta\quad\text{whenever }(j,i)\in E_k,\qquad w_{ii}(k)\ge\eta\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).\] If the selected stochastic convention is row stochastic, additionally \(W_k\mathbf1=\mathbf1\); if it is column stochastic, additionally \(\mathbf1^\top W_k=\mathbf1^\top\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing weights are admissible when their nonzero off-diagonal support follows the available communication edges, every active edge receives a weight bounded below by one common positive constant, and each agent retains a uniformly positive self-weight. The appropriate row- or column-normalization condition is an additional part of the selected mixing convention.
assumptions_latex: \(G_k\) and \(W_k\) share the receiver-by-sender orientation.
A single constant \(\eta>0\) applies uniformly over agents, edges, and time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Active communication and self-loop weights are at least \(\eta\), unsupported off-diagonal weights are zero, and the chosen stochastic normalization holds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For each \(k\), \(\operatorname{supp}(W_k)\setminus\{(i,i)\}\subseteq E_k\), and every positive entry specified by an active edge or self-loop lies in \([\eta,1]\).
special_cases_latex: For a fixed graph and fixed matrix, the condition reduces to a positive minimum over the finitely many required weights.
immediate_consequences_latex: No active communication channel can receive an arbitrarily vanishing fraction of weight.
Positive diagonal entries prevent the mixing dynamics from being forced to update solely from other agents.
boundary_notes: Some analyses require positivity only on a selected spanning subgraph rather than every available edge.
Self-weight positivity is a common aperiodicity condition but is not intrinsic to every communication protocol.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cyclic permutation is strongly connected and doubly stochastic but only rotates agent values, showing that connectivity and stochasticity alone do not guarantee consensus.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((W_k)_{k\ge0}\) be nonnegative \(n\times n\) matrices and define the backward product \(\Phi(k,t):=W_kW_{k-1}\cdots W_t\) for \(k\ge t\). Let \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top/n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A time-varying mixing sequence has uniform long-horizon mixing when every product over a consecutive time interval approaches the arithmetic averaging matrix at a geometric rate whose constants do not depend on the interval's starting time. Double stochasticity selects the arithmetic-average limit.
assumptions_latex: \(W_k\ge0\), \(W_k\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and \(\mathbf1^\top W_k=\mathbf1^\top\) for every \(k\).
The norm is the matrix spectral norm and \(\Phi(k,t)\) uses chronological right-to-left multiplication.

Each entry of \(\Phi(k,t)\) converges uniformly to \(1/n\).

knowledge_statements.title: Static-Graph Connectivity Conditions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed undirected graph must be connected, while a fixed directed graph must be strongly connected, so information can travel between every pair of agents.

Under the convention that \((j,i)\in E\) permits agent \(i\) to receive from agent \(j\), these conditions permit information originating at any agent to reach every other agent.

Communication edges are fixed throughout the execution.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An undirected graph \(G\) is connected if for every \(i,j\in V\) there exists a path joining \(i\) and \(j\). A directed graph \(G\) is strongly connected if for every ordered pair \((i,j)\) there exists a directed path from \(i\) to \(j\). A directed graph is rooted, or contains a directed spanning tree, if there exists \(r\in V\) such that every \(j\in V\) is reachable from \(r\) by a directed path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed undirected network is connected when every two vertices are linked by a path. A fixed directed network is strongly connected when every vertex can reach every other vertex following edge directions. The weaker rooted condition requires only one root that can reach all vertices.

Paths use only edges in the fixed set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Connectivity, strong connectivity, and rootedness are defined by the stated universal or root-based path-reachability conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: An undirected graph is connected if and only if it has exactly one connected component.
A directed graph is strongly connected if and only if its transpose is strongly connected and all vertices lie in one strongly connected component.
A directed graph is rooted if and only if it contains an outward directed spanning tree.
special_cases_latex: For an undirected graph viewed as a bidirected graph, ordinary connectivity and strong connectivity coincide.
immediate_consequences_latex: Strong connectivity implies rootedness.
Rootedness does not require paths from every vertex back to the root.

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodicity of Mixing-Matrix Products
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive stochastic matrices over jointly connected windows make long products geometrically close to a rank-one stochastic matrix, eliminating disagreement even when limiting weights are nonuniform.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated assumptions, there exist constants \(C<\infty\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\), depending only on \(n\), \(B\), and \(\alpha\), such that for every \(t\geq s\), \[\inf_{q\in\Delta_n}\left\|W_{t:s}-\mathbf{1}q^{\mathsf T}\right\|\leq C\rho^{\lfloor (t-s+1)/B\rfloor}.\] Here \(\Delta_n=\{q\in\mathbb{R}^n:q\geq0,\ \mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}q=1\}\), and the norm is any fixed matrix norm, with a corresponding value of \(C\). Thus all rows of a sufficiently long product become equal asymptotically, although their common limiting weights need not be uniform.
assumptions_latex: Every \(W_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is row-stochastic with positive diagonal.
Every positive entry of every \(W_k\) is at least \(\alpha>0\).
The induced directed graph sequence is uniformly \(B\)-jointly strongly connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Products of the mixing matrices approach the rank-one stochastic family geometrically and therefore contract disagreement uniformly.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak and uniform ergodicity of stochastic-matrix products
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((W_k)_{k\ge0}\) be row-stochastic \(n\times n\) matrices, and define \(\Phi(k,t)=W_kW_{k-1}\cdots W_t\) for \(k\ge t\). Let \(\delta(A):=\frac12\max_{i,j}\sum_{\ell=1}^n|a_{i\ell}-a_{j\ell}|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state, time-inhomogeneous row-stochastic products; ergodicity concerns loss of dependence on the receiving row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence is weakly ergodic if, for every fixed \(t\ge0\), \[\delta(\Phi(k,t))\longrightarrow0\qquad(k\to\infty).\] It is uniformly geometrically ergodic if there exist \(C\ge1\) and \(\rho\in[0,1)\) such that \[\delta(\Phi(k,t))\le C\rho^{k-t+1}\qquad\text{for all }k\ge t\ge0.\] Equivalently, weak ergodicity means that any two rows of \(\Phi(k,t)\) approach one another in \(\ell_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence of row-stochastic matrices is weakly ergodic when every long product forgets which receiving row is observed: all rows of the product become asymptotically identical. Uniform geometric ergodicity strengthens this by requiring a common exponential bound for every starting time.
assumptions_latex: Each \(W_k\) is nonnegative and satisfies \(W_k\mathbf1=\mathbf1\).
Products are ordered as \(W_k\cdots W_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak ergodicity is \(\delta(\Phi(k,t))\to0\) for each \(t\); uniform geometric ergodicity is the stated bound with common \(C\) and \(\rho<1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\delta(\Phi(k,t))\to0\) if and only if \(\max_{i,j}\|e_i^\top\Phi(k,t)-e_j^\top\Phi(k,t)\|_1\to0\).
special_cases_latex: For doubly stochastic products, an existing rank-one limit must have identical rows equal to \(\mathbf1^\top/n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For scalar states, \(\max_i(\Phi(k,t)x)_i-\min_i(\Phi(k,t)x)_i\) vanishes under weak ergodicity.
Uniform geometric ergodicity supplies a quantitative disagreement-decay factor.
boundary_notes: Weak ergodicity does not by itself assert convergence of the common row as \(k\to\infty\); that stronger property is often called strong ergodicity.
Column-stochastic products require a transposed or column-oriented formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral and diameter propagation condition measures
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected undirected graph with diameter \(D_G\), Laplacian \(L\), and eigenvalues \(0=\lambda_1(L)<\lambda_2(L)\le\cdots\le\lambda_n(L)\). Let \(W\) be a symmetric doubly stochastic mixing matrix compatible with \(G\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed connected undirected networks; conditioning is summarized by graph diameter, Laplacian spectral ratios, or mixing contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The graph diameter is \[D_G:=\max_{i,j\in V}\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j).\] The Laplacian spectral gap is \(\gamma_L:=\lambda_2(L)\), and the positive-spectrum condition number is \[\kappa_L:=\frac{\lambda_n(L)}{\lambda_2(L)}.\] For symmetric mixing, the disagreement factor and mixing condition scale are \[\rho_W:=\|W-J\|_2=\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i(W)|,\qquad \tau_W:=\frac1{1-\rho_W}\quad\text{when }\rho_W<1.\] These are network-propagation conditioning measures, not one interchangeable scalar definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Network propagation can be conditioned by several related quantities. Diameter measures the longest shortest path. The Laplacian gap measures algebraic connectivity, while the ratio of largest to smallest positive Laplacian eigenvalue is a spectral condition number. For symmetric averaging, the norm of W minus the averaging projector measures one-round disagreement contraction, and its inverse gap gives a mixing scale.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite, undirected, and connected.
\(W=W^\top\), \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and \(\mathbf1^\top W=\mathbf1^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_G\), \(\gamma_L\), \(\kappa_L\), \(\rho_W\), and \(\tau_W\) are defined by the displayed path-length and spectral formulas.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(D_G\) is the least integer \(D\) such that every vertex pair is joined by a path of at most \(D\) edges.
\(\gamma_L=\min_{x\perp\mathbf1,\,x\ne0}x^\top Lx/\|x\|_2^2\).
special_cases_latex: For the complete graph with unweighted Laplacian, \(D_G=1\) and \(\kappa_L=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Smaller \(\rho_W\) gives stronger one-round Euclidean disagreement contraction.
Disconnected graphs have \(\lambda_2(L)=0\), so \(\kappa_L\) is not finite under this definition.
boundary_notes: For nonsymmetric directed mixing, eigenvalue moduli alone need not determine transient contraction.
Diameter and spectral conditioning capture different propagation features and should not be conflated.

Spectral-Gap Measures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absolute spectral gap is one minus the largest nonconsensus eigenvalue magnitude; it quantifies Euclidean contraction of disagreement by one symmetric mixing step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Order the eigenvalues of \(W\) as \(1=\lambda_1(W)\geq\lambda_2(W)\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n(W)\geq-1\). Define \[\rho_\perp=\|W-J\|_2=\max\{|\lambda_2(W)|,|\lambda_n(W)|\},\qquad \gamma=1-\rho_\perp.\] For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\|(W-J)x\|_2\leq\rho_\perp\|(I-J)x\|_2\). Hence \(\gamma>0\) exactly when one mixing step is a strict Euclidean contraction on the disagreement subspace. If \(W\) is positive semidefinite, then \(\rho_\perp=\lambda_2(W)\) and \(\gamma=1-\lambda_2(W)\).
assumptions_latex: The matrix \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and doubly stochastic.
The eigenvalue \(1\) of \(W\) is simple.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The absolute spectral gap \(\gamma=1-\rho_\perp\) measures one-step contraction on the disagreement subspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric doubly stochastic mixing; the absolute gap handles possible negative eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.title: Network Condition Numbers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The network condition number is the ratio of the largest Laplacian eigenvalue to algebraic connectivity, measuring the spectral difficulty of reducing disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(G\) is connected, its Laplacian eigenvalues satisfy \(0=\lambda_1(L)<\lambda_2(L)\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_n(L)=\lambda_{\max}(L)\). For a mixing matrix of the form \(W=I-\eta L\), the admissible step size and resulting disagreement contraction depend on these two extreme nonzero eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.title: Diameter–Mixing Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local communication has finite speed: diameter-separated agents cannot influence each other before D rounds, and their mixing distributions remain disjoint for fewer than half that many rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After \(t\) synchronous neighbor-communication rounds, the state at vertex \(i\) can depend only on initial data at vertices in \(\{j:d_G(i,j)\leq t\}\). Consequently, information from one endpoint of a diameter-realizing path cannot affect the other endpoint before \(D\) rounds. If \(P\) is any row-stochastic matrix supported on self-loops and edges of \(G\), and \(u,v\) satisfy \(d_G(u,v)=D\), then for \(2t<D\) the supports of \(e_u^{\mathsf T}P^t\) and \(e_v^{\mathsf T}P^t\) are disjoint. Their total-variation distance is therefore \(1\), precluding uniform pairwise mixing before \(\lceil D/2\rceil\) rounds.
assumptions_latex: Communication in one round crosses at most one edge of a fixed connected graph \(G\).
The graph diameter is \(D=\max_{i,j}d_G(i,j)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global influence requires at least \(D\) rounds, and pairwise distributional mixing requires at least \(\lceil D/2\rceil\) rounds in the worst case.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-speed relation between graph diameter and local synchronous mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Poor-Connectivity Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connected path networks become increasingly ill-conditioned: their gap shrinks quadratically, and ordinary local mixing needs quadratically many rounds even for constant-factor disagreement reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the path family \((P_n)_{n\geq2}\), the nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues scale as \(\lambda_2(L)=\Theta(n^{-2})\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(L)=\Theta(1)\). Hence \(\kappa_G=\Theta(n^2)\). A symmetric lazy nearest-neighbor mixing matrix with uniformly comparable edge probabilities likewise has absolute spectral gap \(\gamma=\Theta(n^{-2})\). Its disagreement contraction factor is \(1-\Theta(n^{-2})\), so reducing Euclidean disagreement by a factor \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) requires \(\Theta(n^2\log(1/\varepsilon))\) rounds. Thus connectivity alone does not provide dimension-independent propagation or consensus rates.
assumptions_latex: The network is the path graph \(P_n\) with \(n\geq2\).
Mixing uses a symmetric lazy nearest-neighbor stochastic matrix with edge probabilities bounded above and below by positive constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For paths, \(\gamma=\Theta(n^{-2})\), \(\kappa_G=\Theta(n^2)\), and constant-factor disagreement reduction requires \(\Theta(n^2)\) rounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path graphs exhibit a canonical vanishing-gap, ill-conditioned connectivity regime.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every block of a fixed number of consecutive topologies must have a connected union, although individual graphs may be disconnected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The graph sequence \((G_t)_{t\geq0}\), with \(G_t=(V,E_t)\), is uniformly jointly connected with window \(B\) when, for every \(t\geq0\), the union graph \(G_{[t,t+B-1]}=\bigl(V,\bigcup_{s=t}^{t+B-1}E_s\bigr)\) is connected. For directed graphs, the corresponding uniform joint strong-connectivity condition requires every such union digraph to be strongly connected. Individual graphs \(G_t\) may be disconnected; the condition requires paths to be available collectively within every window of the same finite length \(B\).
assumptions_latex: \((G_t)_{t\geq0}\) is a sequence of graphs on a fixed finite vertex set \(V\).
\(B\geq1\) is an integer window length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(t\), the union graph \(\bigl(V,\bigcup_{s=t}^{t+B-1}E_s\bigr)\) is connected, or strongly connected in the directed version.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform sliding-window connectivity for undirected or strongly connected directed graph sequences.

children.title: Neighbor Communication Model
children.top_down_role: Local information-exchange interfaces available to network agents.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At round \(k\), let \(G_k=(V,E_k)\) be a directed communication graph. Agent \(i\) has local state \(s_i^k\in\mathcal S_i\), emits messages in spaces \(\mathcal M_{ij}\), and has in-neighborhood \(N_i^-(k):=\{j:(j,i)\in E_k\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round-based deterministic communication with arbitrary local state and edge-indexed message spaces; computation is local after reception.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A neighbor communication round consists of local encoders and update maps \[m_{ji}^k=E_{ji}^k(s_j^k)\in\mathcal M_{ji}\quad((j,i)\in E_k),\] \[s_i^{k+1}=U_i^k\!\left(s_i^k,(m_{ji}^k)_{j\in N_i^-(k)}\right).\] The locality condition is that \(E_{ji}^k\) depends only on sender \(j\)'s locally available information and \(U_i^k\) depends only on agent \(i\)'s prior local information and messages received along edges entering \(i\) at round \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a neighbor communication model, the graph determines which directed messages may be delivered in each round. Every message is encoded from information locally available to its sender, and every new agent state is computed only from that agent's old state and the messages arriving from its current in-neighbors.
assumptions_latex: Agents are indexed by the fixed finite set \(V\).
An edge \((j,i)\in E_k\) authorizes a message from \(j\) to \(i\) during round \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Messages and state transitions factor through the edge-local encoders \(E_{ji}^k\) and receiver-local update maps \(U_i^k\) shown above.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The global transition map has component \(i\) measurable only with respect to \(s_i^k\) and data received from \(N_i^-(k)\), once any protocol randomness is included in the local state.
special_cases_latex: Linear mixing has \(m_{ji}^k=s_j^k\) and \(s_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}^ks_j^k\).
Broadcast, pairwise gossip, and edge-specific message passing arise by restricting the encoders and active edges.
immediate_consequences_latex: Information from a nonneighbor cannot influence agent \(i\) in one round unless it was previously relayed through local states.
boundary_notes: This definition does not impose bandwidth, delay, loss, privacy, or quantization constraints.
Asynchronous execution requires an event- or delay-indexed interface rather than this synchronous round model.

knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Broadcast Communication
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An agent forms one message and sends that identical payload to all currently available neighbors; receivers may still process received messages differently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A neighborhood broadcast by agent \(i\) at round \(k\) consists of forming one payload \(m_i^k=\phi_i(x_i^k)\) and delivering that identical payload to every \(j\in N_i^{\mathrm{out}}(k)\). The encoder \(\phi_i\) cannot tailor the payload to the recipient within the same broadcast action. After reception, each agent \(j\) may apply a recipient-specific update \(x_j^{k+1}=\psi_j^k(x_j^k,(m_i^k)_{i\in N_j^{\mathrm{in}}(k)})\). Thus broadcast restricts message formation, not how receivers aggregate the messages they obtain.
assumptions_latex: At round \(k\), agent \(i\) has state \(x_i^k\) and available out-neighbors \(N_i^{\mathrm{out}}(k)\).
A transmitted message is delivered reliably to every currently available out-neighbor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One broadcast action sends the same message \(m_i^k\) to every agent in \(N_i^{\mathrm{out}}(k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous reliable local broadcast with identical payloads for all available recipients.

notation.meaning: message formed by agent i at round k

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G_k=(V,E_k)\) be a directed graph at round \(k\), with out-neighborhood \(N_j^+(k):=\{i:(j,i)\in E_k\}\). Agent \(j\) has local state \(s_j^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous one-to-many communication in which a sender cannot tailor payloads to individual recipients during the same broadcast.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A neighborhood broadcast protocol uses, for each sender \(j\) and round \(k\), one encoder \[m_j^k=B_j^k(s_j^k)\in\mathcal M_j\] and delivers the identical payload \(m_j^k\) to every receiver \(i\in N_j^+(k)\). Each receiver updates by \[s_i^{k+1}=U_i^k\!\left(s_i^k,(m_j^k)_{j\in N_i^-(k)}\right).\] The defining broadcast constraint is \(m_{ji}^k=m_j^k\) for all \(i\in N_j^+(k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Neighborhood broadcast is a one-to-many interface: during one round, each sender forms one message from its local state, and exactly that same message is made available to all of its active out-neighbors. Receivers may still process received messages differently through their own local update maps.
assumptions_latex: The graph specifies the active recipients of each sender at each round.
A broadcast payload has a common message space \(\mathcal M_j\) for all recipients of sender \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every sender \(j\), round \(k\), and recipients \(i,i'\in N_j^+(k)\), \(m_{ji}^k=m_{ji'}^k=B_j^k(s_j^k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The family of edge encoders leaving \(j\) factors through one common encoder: \(E_{ji}^k=B_j^k\) on every active outgoing edge.
special_cases_latex: Broadcasting the current iterate uses \(B_j^k(s_j^k)=x_j^k\).
A wireless broadcast may realize the common-message constraint physically, while a wired system may emulate it by repeated identical transmissions.
immediate_consequences_latex: The sender-side payload cannot contain recipient-specific information unless that information is encoded in a common message delivered to all recipients.
boundary_notes: Different delivery times, erasures, or receiver noise require additional channel variables.
Sending separately tailored messages on distinct outgoing edges is edge-local message passing, not broadcast under this definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Gossip Communication
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round, one selected neighboring pair replaces both values by their average while all other agents remain unchanged; adequate repeated edge activation yields average consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize arbitrary states \(x_1^0,\ldots,x_n^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At round \(k\), select an edge \(\{i_k,j_k\}\) according to a specified schedule or probability distribution and perform \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}=x_{j_k}^{k+1}=\frac{x_{i_k}^k+x_{j_k}^k}{2},\qquad x_\ell^{k+1}=x_\ell^k\ \text{for }\ell\notin\{i_k,j_k\}.\] Stop under a prescribed round budget or disagreement tolerance and output the current local states. Every update preserves \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^k\); convergence to the initial average additionally requires a selection rule that activates sufficient edges repeatedly.
assumptions_latex: At round \(k\), an edge \(\{i_k,j_k\}\) is selected from an undirected graph.
Only the selected endpoints communicate during that round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected pair replaces its values by their average, preserving the global sum and contracting their local disagreement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical randomized or scheduled pairwise averaging update on an undirected graph.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). At round \(k\), an edge \(e_k=\{i_k,j_k\}\in E\) is selected, and agents hold states \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\).
