knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pairwise averaging gossip step with parameter \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\) is \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)x_{i_k}^k+\alpha_kx_{j_k}^k,\qquad x_{j_k}^{k+1}=\alpha_kx_{i_k}^k+(1-\alpha_k)x_{j_k}^k,\] with \(x_\ell^{k+1}=x_\ell^k\) for \(\ell\notin\{i_k,j_k\}\). In stacked form, \[X^{k+1}=(W_{e_k}(\alpha_k)\otimes I_d)X^k,\quad W_{\{i,j\}}(\alpha)=I_n-\alpha(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^\top.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pairwise gossip round selects one communication edge. Its two endpoints exchange their states and replace them by symmetric convex combinations, while every other agent remains unchanged. The corresponding matrix is identity except on the selected two-agent block.
assumptions_latex: The selected pair \(\{i_k,j_k\}\) is an edge of the communication graph.
\(0\le\alpha_k\le1\), and both endpoints use the same parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only the selected endpoint states change, according to the displayed symmetric averaging equations.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The selected two-state sum is invariant: \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}+x_{j_k}^{k+1}=x_{i_k}^k+x_{j_k}^k\).
\(W_e(\alpha)\) is doubly stochastic for \(\alpha\in[0,1]\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\alpha_k=1/2\), both endpoints adopt their arithmetic mean.
For \(\alpha_k=0\), the selected communication produces no state change.
immediate_consequences_latex: The global arithmetic average is preserved at every pairwise step.
Randomized gossip is obtained by sampling \(e_k\) from a specified distribution on \(E\).

Convergence requires persistent edge activation or suitable probabilistic assumptions, which are not part of the communication primitive.

children.title: Edge-Local Message Passing

knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Local Message Passing
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each active edge may carry its own recipient-specific message, allowing agents to communicate edge variables, coupling information, or distinct residuals to different neighbors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In an edge-local message-passing round, each active directed edge \((i,j)\in E_k\) carries a payload \(m_{i\to j}^k=\phi_{ij}^k(x_i^k,z_{ij}^k)\), where \(z_{ij}^k\) is optional edge-local state. Payloads associated with two different outgoing edges may differ even when they have the same sender. Agent \(j\) updates according to \(x_j^{k+1}=\psi_j^k(x_j^k,(m_{i\to j}^k)_{i:(i,j)\in E_k})\). This model represents edge-specific coupling data, dual variables, or residuals and strictly contains identical-payload neighborhood broadcast as a special case.
assumptions_latex: Each directed edge \((i,j)\) active at round \(k\) can carry one edge-indexed payload.
Agent updates use only their local state and payloads received on incident active edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Edge-local communication permits distinct payloads \(m_{i\to j}^k\) for different neighbors \(j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous edge-indexed messages with recipient-dependent payloads.

notation.meaning: message sent from i to j at round k

A receiver updates from its prior state and incoming messages.
assumptions_latex: An edge \((j,i)\in E_k\) authorizes transmission only from \(j\) to \(i\).
All domains and codomains of \(E_{ji}^k\), \(U_i^k\), and \(Q_{ji}^k\) are fixed by the corresponding local state spaces.

In an incidence representation, the collection \((m_{ji}^k)_{(j,i)\in E_k}\) is an edge-indexed vector whose aggregation at node \(i\) uses only incoming-edge coordinates.

Broadcast is the restricted case in which all messages leaving one sender are identical.

knowledge_statements.title: Stateful Neighbor Communication
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents retain auxiliary state between rounds and use it when forming messages and updates; trackers, cached estimates, and error-feedback residuals are instances of this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stateful neighbor-communication mechanism has the local state-space form \[m_{i\to j}^k=H_{ij}^k(x_i^k,z_i^k),\qquad (x_i^{k+1},z_i^{k+1})=F_i^k\left(x_i^k,z_i^k,(m_{j\to i}^k)_{j\in N_i^{\mathrm{in}}(k)}\right).\] The auxiliary variable \(z_i^k\) persists between rounds and is initialized by a specified value \(z_i^0\). Memoryless communication is recovered when \(z_i^k\) is absent or constant. Gradient trackers, compression residuals, and cached neighbor estimates fit this representation by choosing the state space and maps \(H_{ij}^k\) and \(F_i^k\) appropriately.
assumptions_latex: Each agent \(i\) stores a persistent local memory \(z_i^k\) in addition to its primary state \(x_i^k\).
Messages are exchanged only along edges active at round \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stateful communication updates both the primary state and persistent memory from current local information and received neighbor messages.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic state-space representation encompassing trackers, memories, residual accumulators, and error-feedback states.

notation.meaning: message sent from i to j

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stateful neighbor-communication process consists of message maps \(M_{ij}^k:\mathcal S_i\times\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal M_{ij}\) and transition maps \(T_i^k:\mathcal S_i\times\mathcal D_i\times\prod_{j\in N_i^-(k)}\mathcal M_{ji}\to\mathcal S_i\) such that, for every \(k\ge0\), \(m_{ij}^k=M_{ij}^k(s_i^k,d_i^k)\) is sent only when \((i,j)\in E_k\), and \(s_i^{k+1}=T_i^k(s_i^k,d_i^k,(m_{ji}^k)_{j\in N_i^-(k)})\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round, every agent forms edge-local messages from its retained state and current data, receives messages only from in-neighbors, and updates its retained state through a local transition map. The model is stateful precisely when retained information can affect a later message or transition beyond what current inputs and current received messages determine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_{ij}^k=M_{ij}^k(s_i^k,d_i^k),\qquad s_i^{k+1}=T_i^k\!\left(s_i^k,d_i^k,(m_{ji}^k)_{j\in N_i^-(k)}\right).\)

children.title: Distributed Coordination Architectures
children.top_down_role: Centralized, peer-to-peer, hierarchical, and federated coordination arrangements.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordination architecture of a distributed optimization system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) index computing agents, let \(C\) be a possibly empty set of coordinator processes, and let \(P=V\cup C\). At round \(k\), process \(p\in P\) has state \(s_p^k\in\mathcal S_p\), receives messages along a directed graph \(G^k=(P,E^k)\), and applies a state-transition map.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The object defined is the information-flow and authority structure of an iterative optimization system, independently of the particular objective, update formula, synchronization convention, or convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coordination architecture is a tuple \[\mathfrak A=(P,V,C,(G^k)_{k\ge0},(\mathcal M_{pq})_{p,q\in P},(U_p^k)_{p\in P,k\ge0}),\] where a message \(m_{pq}^k\in\mathcal M_{pq}\) may be sent only if \((p,q)\in E^k\), and every process evolves according to \[s_p^{k+1}=U_p^k\!\left(s_p^k,\{m_{qp}^k:(q,p)\in E^k\}\right).\] Its architectural class is determined by which processes may aggregate information and issue coordination variables: centralized when one distinguished \(c\in C\) mediates all inter-agent coordination, peer-to-peer when \(C=\varnothing\), hierarchical when coordinator processes form multiple tiers, and federated when a coordinator exists but each agent's raw local dataset is excluded from the permitted message spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordination architecture specifies the processes, time-indexed communication edges, permitted message spaces, and local state-transition maps of a distributed optimization system. Centralized, peer-to-peer, hierarchical, and federated architectures are distinguished by the presence and organization of coordinators and by the information that messages are allowed to disclose.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak A\) is classified by \(C\), the coordinator subgraph, and the admissible message spaces \((\mathcal M_{pq})\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For synchronous deterministic systems, all maps \(U_p^k\) may be combined into one global transition \(s^{k+1}=U^k(s^k)\) whose block-sparsity is prescribed by \(G^k\).
special_cases_latex: A star graph with one center in \(C\) gives centralized aggregation.
Taking \(C=\varnothing\) and allowing only neighbor messages gives a peer-to-peer architecture.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two algorithms with identical numerical updates can have different coordination architectures if their allowed information paths differ.
The architecture alone does not determine communication complexity because message sizes and activation schedules remain separate data.
boundary_notes: A logical coordinator may be implemented by several machines; the definition concerns roles and information flow rather than physical hardware.
Privacy, security, and fault tolerance are not implied merely by restricting message spaces.

notation.meaning: State-transition map of process \(p\) at round \(k\).

children.title: Centralized Aggregation Architectures

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,ldots,m\}\) be worker agents and let \(c\notin V\) be a distinguished aggregation process. Worker \(i\) has state \(x_i^k\), produces an uplink message \(u_i^k\), and receives a downlink message \(d_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a logical star-coordination model. It permits parallel local computation but requires all cross-worker coordination to pass through a distinguished service.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed iterative system has a centralized aggregation architecture if, for every round \(k\), there are maps \(P_i^k\), \(A^k\), and \(Q_i^k\) such that \[u_i^k=P_i^k(x_i^k),\qquad a^k=A^k(u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k),\qquad d_i^k=Q_i^k(a^k),\] and each worker updates by \[x_i^{k+1}=U_i^k(x_i^k,d_i^k),\] with no worker-to-worker message entering any \(U_i^k\) directly. Equivalently, after deleting self-loops, every directed communication path from one worker to another contains \(c\). The aggregate \(a^k\) may be a sum, average, model parameter, dual variable, or other sufficient coordination object.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a centralized aggregation architecture, each worker sends a locally produced message to one distinguished service. That service combines the worker messages and returns coordination information used in the next local updates. No direct worker message participates in another worker's update; every cross-worker information path passes through the aggregator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall i\ne j)\), every information path from worker \(i\) to worker \(j\) passes through \(c\), and the round transition factors through \(A^k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The communication graph is a directed subgraph of the bidirected star on \(V\cup\{c\}\), possibly with self-loops.
The global worker transition factors as \(x^{k+1}=U^k(x^k,Q^k(A^k(P^k(x^k))))\) with block-separable \(P^k,Q^k,U^k\).
special_cases_latex: Parameter-server averaging uses \(a^k=\sum_i w_i u_i^k\) with \(w_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_iw_i=1\).
A master process that allocates a shared resource via a dual price is a centralized aggregation architecture.
immediate_consequences_latex: The aggregator is an articulation point of the logical inter-worker information graph.
Centralization of coordination does not require centralization of local objective evaluation.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require workers to participate synchronously.
Replication of the aggregation service for availability is compatible only when replicas collectively implement the same distinguished logical role.
review_flags: No inspected source precisely establishes the stated factorization and graph characterization.
knowledge_statements.title: Centralized aggregation architecture
Central-Coordinator Architectures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers compute local messages from the shared state, while a persistent coordinator aggregates every contribution and broadcasts the next state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A central-coordinator architecture consists of workers \(1,\ldots,m\), a coordinator state \(x^k\), worker message maps \(M_i^k\), and a coordinator aggregation map \(A^k\). At round \(k\),
\[u_i^k=M_i^k(x^k;\mathcal D_i),\qquad x^{k+1}=A^k(x^k,u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k),\]
after which the coordinator broadcasts \(x^{k+1}\) or designated blocks to the workers. Workers need not communicate directly; every contribution to the shared iterate passes logically through the persistent coordinator.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Server Architectures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Servers own parameter blocks; workers pull parameter versions, compute local-data updates, and push them for barrier-synchronized batch application or asynchronous application that may accept stale reads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A parameter-server architecture maintains server-resident parameter blocks \(x_{(1)},\ldots,x_{(q)}\). Worker \(i\) pulls a version \(x^{\tau_i(k)}\), computes \(u_i^k=U_i(x^{\tau_i(k)};\mathcal D_i)\), and pushes the update to the responsible server blocks. A server may apply one received update as
\[x^{k+1}=S^k(x^k,u_i^k)\]
or aggregate a batch of concurrently received updates. Execution is synchronous when workers use the designated round-\(k\) version and update application is separated by a round barrier; it is stale-read asynchronous when updates computed from \(\tau_i(k)<k\) may be accepted without such a global barrier.
assumptions_latex: Every parameter block has a designated server owner.
Worker \(i\) computes from local data \(\mathcal D_i\) and a pulled parameter version.
Synchronous execution uses a round barrier in addition to current-version reads.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^{\tau_i(k)},u_i^k,S^k)\), together with the update-application schedule, specifies the pull-compute-push parameter-server cycle.

knowledge_statements.title: Worker–Aggregator Topologies
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bipartite graph specifies worker-to-aggregator communication; one aggregator gives a star, while multiple aggregators require reconciliation of their outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W\) be a set of workers and \(A\) a set of aggregators. A worker–aggregator topology is the bipartite graph \(G=(W\cup A,E)\), where \((i,a)\in E\) exactly when worker \(i\) may send a local message to aggregator \(a\). For messages \(u_i^k\), aggregator \(a\) computes
\[v_a^k=\mathcal A_a^k\bigl((u_i^k)_{i\in N(a)}\bigr).\]
A single-star topology has \(|A|=1\) and \(N(a)=W\); multiple aggregators partition or overlap worker neighborhoods and require an additional rule to reconcile \((v_a^k)_{a\in A}\).
assumptions_latex: Messages travel only along edges in \(E\).
Every participating worker has at least one adjacent aggregator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G=(W\cup A,E)\) determines the admissible aggregation neighborhoods \(N(a)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Central-Service Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because every worker message crosses one service, fixed service bandwidth and processing capacity force synchronous round time to grow at least linearly with workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(m\) workers each send and receive \(s\) bits through one central service during every synchronous round. The service must process at least \(2ms\) incident bits per round. If its aggregate ingress-plus-egress rate is at most \(B\) bits per unit time and it processes at most \(P\) worker messages per unit time, then the round duration satisfies
\[T_{\mathrm{round}}\ge\max\left\{\frac{2ms}{B},\frac{2m}{P}\right\}.\]
Consequently, with fixed \(B\), \(P\), and \(s\), central-service communication time grows at least linearly with the worker count.
assumptions_latex: Every synchronous round requires one upload and one download of \(s>0\) bits per worker.
The central service has total traffic rate \(B>0\) and message-processing rate \(P>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{round}}\ge\max\{2ms/B,2m/P\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-round communication and service-time lower bounds caused by routing all worker traffic through one central service.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the bottleneck leaf and the counting argument is plausible under the stated capacity model, but the cited architecture sections do not establish the exact max lower bound or clarify that P counts both uploads and downloads. A direct locator supporting this capacity model is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Peer-to-Peer Decentralized Architectures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each peer stores and updates a local state using local information and neighbor messages, while no distinguished permanent service exclusively performs global aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a communication graph and let iterations be indexed by \(k\in\mathbb{N}\). A peer-to-peer decentralized architecture assigns a state \(x_i^k\) and local information \(\mathcal D_i\) to each node \(i\in V\), with updates of the form
\[x_i^{k+1}=U_i^k\bigl(x_i^k,(x_j^{\tau_{ij}(k)})_{j\in N_i};\mathcal D_i\bigr),\qquad 0\le\tau_{ij}(k)\le k.\]
Nodes exchange states only along edges of \(G\), and no distinguished permanent service has exclusive responsibility for aggregating all contributions or determining a global iterate. In linear mixing,
\[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j\in V}w_{ij}x_j^k,\qquad w_{ij}=0\quad\text{whenever }j\notin N_i\cup\{i\}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) specifies admissible peer-to-peer communication.
\(k\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(0\le\tau_{ij}(k)\le k\) for every received neighbor state.
Each update uses only the node's local information and received neighbor states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The architecture has no distinguished permanent aggregation service, and communication is local to \(G\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighbor-exchange architecture with local states and no permanent node responsible for global aggregation.

children.top_down_role: Coordination across clusters, edge tiers, or regional aggregators.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite set of processes partitioned into nonempty tiers \(P_0,\ldots,P_L\), where \(P_0\) contains leaf agents and \(L\ge2\). Let \(\pi:P_0\cup\cdots\cup P_{L-1}\to P_1\cup\cdots\cup P_L\) assign each nonroot process a parent in the next tier.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition models logical aggregation and dissemination across at least two coordinator levels; tiers may represent clusters, edge servers, regions, or organizational domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coordination architecture is an \(L\)-tier hierarchy if \(L\ge2\), \(\pi(P_\ell)\subseteq P_{\ell+1}\), repeated application of \(\pi\) reaches a root in \(P_L\), and inter-tier messages follow parent-child edges. For each coordinator \(q\in P_{\ell+1}\), its upward summary has the form \[u_q^k=A_q^k\!\left(s_q^k,\{u_p^k:\pi(p)=q\}\right),\] while downward coordination is recursively disseminated by \[d_p^k=D_p^k(s_p^k,d_{\pi(p)}^k,u_{\pi(p)}^k).\] Thus information from distinct leaves is first combined at their least common ancestral coordinator before reaching higher tiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multi-tier hierarchy partitions processes into leaf and coordinator levels connected by a parent map. Local summaries move upward and are aggregated at each successive level, while coordination information moves downward through the same hierarchy. There must be at least two coordinator levels, distinguishing this family from a single centralized aggregator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi(P_\ell)\subseteq P_{\ell+1}\) and every leaf-to-root coordination path traverses the successive tiers \(P_1,\ldots,P_L\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The parent edges form a rooted forest whose leaves contain \(P_0\), whose roots lie in \(P_L\), and whose internal vertices occupy the intermediate tiers.
special_cases_latex: Clients, edge servers, and a cloud service form a two-coordinator-tier hierarchy with \(L=2\).
Regional aggregators followed by a national aggregator constitute a hierarchy when regional summaries, rather than all raw leaf messages, enter the top-tier update.
immediate_consequences_latex: A coordinator can aggregate a subtree without exposing each descendant's individual message to higher tiers.
Communication and aggregation delays can differ by tier without changing the architecture's defining parent relation.
boundary_notes: A flat star with only one coordinator tier is excluded by \(L\ge2\).
Cross-tier or peer links may supplement the hierarchy, but if they replace the parent-mediated coordination structure the system falls outside this definition.

notation.meaning: Parent map from each nonroot process to the next coordination tier.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents are partitioned into clusters; cluster coordinators aggregate locally and communicate through a top-level coordinator to solve a shared optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A clustered coordination hierarchy is a communication architecture \(\mathcal H=(V,\{c_k\}_{k=1}^K,c_0)\) in which every agent \(i\in V_k\) exchanges optimization messages only within \(V_k\) or with its cluster coordinator \(c_k\), while each \(c_k\) exchanges aggregate messages with the top-level coordinator \(c_0\). knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Tier Information Flow
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hierarchical information flow is cross-tier when every upward aggregate and downward feedback message factors through adjacent tiers, with no nonadjacent bypass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cross-tier information flow is admissible when optimization information moves only through adjacent-tier maps. For upward messages, \(s_{l+1}^t=U_l^t(s_l^t)\) for \(l=0,\ldots,L-1\); for downward messages, \(q_l^t=D_l^t(q_{l+1}^t,s_l^t)\). Thus the upward dependence factors through \(U_{L-1}^t\circ\cdots\circ U_0^t\), and downward feedback factors through \(D_0^t\circ\cdots\circ D_{L-1}^t\). No state at tier \(l\) may directly influence a nonadjacent tier except through these compositions. This condition distinguishes genuine hierarchical flow from a nominal hierarchy containing bypass communication links.
assumptions_latex: The coordination system has tiers \(0,1,\ldots,L\), with tier \(0\) lowest.
Messages passed between adjacent tiers belong to specified finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid cross-tier flow factors as \(U=U_{L-1}\circ\cdots\circ U_0\) upward and \(D=D_0\circ\cdots\circ D_{L-1}\) downward.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adjacent-tier factorization condition for hierarchical optimization messages.
